I can tell I'm one of the elders here by the other stories of procrastination. I'll share mine with you. It all started back when I was a teenager and I was introduced to computer games.

It started with Sim City. A truly addicting game for someone like me. I had been a lego builder as long as I can remember. I had been doing it since I was 3-4. By the time I was 10 I was building some pretty badass stuff and all I wanted was more legos. Call it an obsession if you want but I see it as my first step in using my imagination to build things.

Sim city and video game came into my life and killed that. Why spend countless hours building legos when I could play a game where I could build an entire city. I was hooked. It was nearly the only thing I thought about for almost a decade. I wanted to make the cities perfect. I found Age of Empires and Civ. Now I could control armies and they would do my every command. The power was absolute, as long as I stayed focused on the screen. I could control this world and I tried to be in the computer as often as I could.

This lasted well into my mid 20s. I had many opportunities come and go through those years. Many different pats were laid out befor me and yet I chose to hole up in my dorm or apartment and let them pass me by. I became afraid of doing anything but procrastinating. I dropped out of college and found jobs that suited my lifestyle. Any job that I didn't have to think about when I got home. I would game until I couldn't stay awake any more.

Got married to my long time girlfriend. Then I finally started down the path that I had want to be since I was as young as I could remember. I wanted to be a Father. Not just any father, I wanted to be the best . I waned my kids to be happy and come running at me when they wee me to give me a big hug. I wanted to raise them in my OWN way. I wanted to have some of the things I didn't have.

My first was born in 2009. I still hadn't kicked my addiction to gaming and procrastinating my life away. I would find any free time I could to game. He would lay down for a nap and I would quietly sneak into the computer room for as much game time as possible. Even after my second son came, I still tried to keep the other lifestyle alive. My wife would leave for the weekend and I would binge instead of doing housework or taking time to build things again.

Somewhere between number 2 and 3 the cracks really started to show. All of my wasted time was haunting me day and night. I couldn't run any more. Everything I was seeing was pointing to how procrastinating/addiction almost ruined my life. It still took a few more months till I finally decided to go cold turkey one day. It was hard for a few weeks, the constant itching to hop back on the computer.

A few things saved me. My family, my childhood dreams, and some random people on the internet :). I started going to reddit and reading peoples stories about gaming addiction. It helped a lot. I started trying out new hobbies. My favourite hobby now is Gardening! Who needs video games when you can garden and grow your own food. Who needs video games when REALITY is the ULTIMATE VIDEO GAME!

This life is your only chance to do all the things you want to do. If you spend your life hiding from it, you will regret it.
